task_2.title: Harden lazy-wheel against broken negative range responses
task_2.description: The 1.8.2 update makes lazy wheel metadata fetching more robust when a package index mishandles HTTP suffix range requests. Instead of trusting malformed tail responses from servers such as Artifactory, the library now treats those responses as unsupported negative-range behavior, falls back to a safer path, and remembers that the domain should not use negative ranges.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that lazy wheel metadata inspection continues to work when an index server incorrectly handles HTTP range requests with negative offsets, instead of accepting malformed tail responses or failing the inspection flow.

expectation.grounded: When `lazy-wheel` performs a negative-offset HTTP range request while inspecting a wheel, it should treat the response as invalid negative-range support if the returned `Content-Length` exceeds the requested tail chunk size or if `Content-Range` reports a range starting with a negative byte position. In those cases, the tail fragment should be discarded, the domain should be recorded as not supporting negative ranges, and wheel metadata retrieval should continue through the fallback behavior rather than relying on the malformed negative-range response.
expectation.conceptual: If a package index responds incorrectly to suffix range requests, wheel metadata lookup should recover automatically by falling back to a compatible retrieval path and should keep working without exposing protocol quirks to the user.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing lazy-wheel behavior for repositories that return valid suffix-range responses. Limit the new fallback trigger to clearly invalid negative-range responses, and keep the domain-level compatibility tracking so the client does not repeatedly retry broken negative-range requests against the same host.
constraints.conceptual: Do not degrade normal lazy metadata fetching for compliant repositories. Only treat obviously broken suffix-range behavior as incompatible, and avoid repeating the same failing request pattern once a repository has been identified as incompatible.

behavior: A negative-offset range response is considered invalid for lazy-wheel tail fetching when it returns more bytes than the requested tail chunk implies.
A negative-offset range response is considered invalid for lazy-wheel tail fetching when its reported byte range starts with a negative position.
When either invalid response pattern is detected, lazy-wheel ignores the returned tail payload and classifies the domain as not supporting negative range requests.
After classifying a domain as incompatible with negative ranges, lazy-wheel uses fallback handling for that domain instead of continuing to trust negative-offset range responses.
acceptance_criteria: When wheel metadata is fetched from an index that returns an oversized response to a suffix range request, the metadata lookup should fall back and continue instead of consuming that malformed tail response.

When wheel metadata is fetched from an index that reports a negative starting byte in the suffix range metadata, the client should treat negative ranges as unsupported for that domain and continue through fallback behavior.
When a repository returns valid suffix-range responses, lazy-wheel should continue its normal lazy metadata retrieval behavior without triggering the new fallback.
Once a domain has been identified as mishandling negative suffix ranges, later lazy-wheel metadata requests to that domain should avoid depending on negative suffix range handling.

task_1.title: Harden lazy-wheel fallback for misbehaving package indexes
task_1.description: Poetry 1.8.2 makes lazy-wheel metadata retrieval more tolerant of package indexes that mishandle HTTP range requests. Instead of surfacing unexpected low-level failures or relying on incomplete range metadata, Poetry now classifies these cases as unsupported lazy-wheel behavior and disables lazy-wheel for the affected host so metadata retrieval can fall back safely.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that lazy-wheel metadata retrieval gracefully falls back when a package index mishandles ranged wheel requests, including missing range metadata and other unexpected lazy-wheel failures, so package metadata resolution does not fail simply because lazy-wheel was attempted.

expectation.grounded: `metadata_from_wheel_url` should normalize lazy-wheel failure modes under `LazyWheelUnsupportedError`, including explicit range-support failures, invalid or unsupported wheels, missing `Content-Range` headers needed to determine wheel length, and unexpected exceptions raised while attempting lazy-wheel retrieval. `HTTPRepository` should treat any `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` from wheel metadata lookup as a signal to stop using lazy-wheel for that index host, emit a debug log for the disablement, and continue through the repository fallback path rather than exposing an internal range-handling failure.
expectation.conceptual: When a package index does not correctly support byte-range access for wheel files, Poetry should treat lazy-wheel as unavailable for that source and continue through a safe fallback path. Users should see controlled fallback behavior instead of an unexpected failure caused by malformed, incomplete, or inconsistent range responses.

constraints.grounded: Successful lazy-wheel metadata extraction against compliant servers must continue to return the same metadata. A `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable` response may only be used to infer wheel length when it includes a usable `Content-Range` header. Invalid or corrupt wheels should remain distinguishable as `InvalidWheel`, now within the `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` family. A lazy-wheel failure must not erase previously established knowledge that the same host supports range requests for other URLs.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change behavior for indexes that already behave correctly. Apply fallback conservatively: only disable lazy-wheel when the server response is incomplete, contradictory, or otherwise unsuitable, and do not let one failure broadly regress sources that have already proven compatible.

behavior: `metadata_from_wheel_url` now reports unsupported lazy-wheel situations through the `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` hierarchy instead of allowing unexpected exceptions to escape directly.
If the ranged response used to determine wheel length does not include `Content-Range`, lazy-wheel retrieval is treated as unsupported.
A `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable` response is only used to determine wheel length when the response provides `Content-Range`; otherwise it is not treated as sufficient range metadata.

`HTTPRepository` now disables lazy-wheel support for the affected index host when wheel metadata lookup raises `LazyWheelUnsupportedError`, rather than only when a narrower range-unsupported exception is raised.
Existing invalid or unsupported wheel conditions still surface as dedicated lazy-wheel-related errors, but they now participate in a common unsupported-error family for consistent caller handling.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry requests wheel metadata from an index that omits `Content-Range` in a ranged response needed to determine file length, it should treat lazy-wheel as unsupported for that source instead of failing with an unrelated internal exception.

When a server returns `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable` without a usable `Content-Range` header, Poetry should not infer wheel size from that response and should fall back from lazy-wheel handling.
When an unexpected exception occurs during `metadata_from_wheel_url` lazy-wheel processing, callers should receive a `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` rather than a raw unexpected exception type.

When `HTTPRepository` encounters `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` while extracting package info from a wheel URL, it should disable lazy-wheel for that host and continue metadata handling via the non-lazy fallback path.
When an index correctly supports ranged wheel access and the wheel is valid, lazy-wheel metadata extraction should continue to succeed without behavioral regression.

task_3.title: Handle misleading HTTP range support in lazy-wheel
task_3.description: The 1.8.2 update hardens lazy wheel metadata retrieval against package indexes that claim to support HTTP byte ranges but return the wrong amount of data for ranged requests. Instead of failing with a generic internal assertion, the lazy-wheel path now treats this as an explicit unsupported condition with a dedicated error classification.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that lazy wheel metadata retrieval correctly detects package index servers that advertise HTTP byte-range support but do not honor ranged responses, and report that condition as an explicit unsupported lazy-wheel failure instead of surfacing an internal assertion-style crash.

expectation.grounded: In `poetry.inspection.lazy_wheel`, unsupported lazy-wheel conditions should be represented by `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` and its subclasses. When a ranged GET used by lazy-wheel returns successfully but the response `Content-Length` does not equal the requested byte span, the operation should raise `HTTPRangeRequestNotRespected`. Existing unsupported conditions such as `HTTPRangeRequestUnsupported`, `UnsupportedWheel`, and `InvalidWheel` should remain within the same lazy-wheel unsupported error family.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry lazily reads wheel metadata over HTTP, a server that falsely claims byte-range support should be detected and treated as an unsupported lazy-fetch scenario. Users should receive a deliberate lazy-wheel error classification for that condition rather than an unexpected internal failure.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the normal lazy-wheel success path for compliant ranged responses. Only treat the request as not respected when the returned payload length differs from the requested range length after a successful HTTP response. Preserve the distinction between transport/range-support failures and wheel-content validity issues while keeping them in the lazy-wheel unsupported exception hierarchy.
constraints.conceptual: Keep correct range-based metadata reads working as before, and only flag servers that return the wrong amount of data for a ranged request. Do not blur malformed wheel content errors with HTTP range-behavior problems.

behavior: Lazy-wheel unsupported outcomes are grouped under a shared `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` exception category.
If a ranged HTTP response succeeds but returns a `Content-Length` different from the requested byte count, lazy-wheel raises `HTTPRangeRequestNotRespected`.
The misleading range-support case is surfaced as an explicit lazy-wheel unsupported error instead of relying on a generic assertion failure.
Ranged responses that return the exact requested byte count continue through the existing streaming path without changed behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a wheel URL served by an index that advertises byte-range support, when lazy-wheel issues a ranged request and the server returns a different payload length than requested, then the operation should fail with `HTTPRangeRequestNotRespected`.
When the same mismatch occurs, it should be observable as part of the `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` family rather than as an internal assertion-style failure.
When a server honors the requested byte range and returns the exact requested length, lazy-wheel metadata retrieval should continue normally.
When lazy-wheel encounters other unsupported or invalid wheel conditions, they should remain classified within the lazy-wheel unsupported exception hierarchy.

task_4.title: Support redirected HEAD requests in lazy-wheel
task_4.description: Poetry 1.8.2 fixes lazy-wheel metadata inspection for wheel URLs that redirect before serving the artifact. The initial remote metadata probe now follows redirects so redirected repositories and CDNs can still be inspected lazily, while the resolved response must still satisfy the existing success and byte-range requirements.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that lazy-wheel can inspect wheel metadata when the wheel URL redirects on the initial HEAD request instead of failing before reaching the actual artifact location.

expectation.grounded: When lazy-wheel performs the initial HEAD request used by metadata_from_wheel_url and LazyFileOverHTTP, it should follow HTTP redirects and evaluate the final response. If the resolved HEAD response is successful and advertises byte-range support, lazy-wheel should continue remote metadata extraction normally.
expectation.conceptual: Wheel metadata lookup should work for redirected artifact URLs the same way it works for direct URLs, provided the resolved download endpoint is valid for lazy inspection.

constraints.grounded: This change must not relax existing lazy-wheel validation on the resolved response: final HTTP errors should still fail, and artifacts that do not support byte ranges should still be rejected through the existing lazy-wheel failure behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Following redirects should only remove redirect-related failures. All existing eligibility checks for lazily reading a remote wheel must still apply after the redirect is resolved.

behavior: The initial HEAD request used by lazy-wheel to determine remote wheel properties follows HTTP redirects.
A wheel URL that redirects to the actual artifact location remains eligible for lazy metadata extraction if the resolved response is successful and supports byte ranges.
Status validation and range-support validation are applied to the final resolved HEAD response, not only to the original URL.
acceptance_criteria: When metadata_from_wheel_url is given a wheel URL that responds with an HTTP redirect before the file is served, it should still return metadata if the resolved endpoint responds successfully and supports byte-range access.
When a wheel URL is served directly without redirects, lazy-wheel behavior should remain unchanged.
When the resolved redirect target returns an unsuccessful response, lazy-wheel should still fail through its existing HTTP error behavior.
When the resolved redirect target does not support byte-range access, lazy-wheel should still reject lazy inspection through its existing unsupported-range behavior.

task_6.title: Correct metadata hash validation for charset-ambiguous responses
task_6.description: Poetry 1.8.2 fixes metadata hash verification for package metadata responses whose text decoding can differ from the original payload bytes. This prevents valid metadata from being treated as mismatched when a repository omits charset information and the decoded text would not round-trip to the same bytes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that metadata file hash verification uses the exact response payload so metadata served without reliable charset information does not fail validation because of encoding-related byte changes.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry verifies a downloaded metadata file against its declared metadata hash during repository access, the hash calculation should be based on the raw HTTP response body bytes rather than a decoded and re-encoded text representation. Metadata responses from indexes that do not provide charset information should still compare correctly against published metadata hashes if the original bytes match.
expectation.conceptual: Metadata integrity checks should reflect the actual file that was downloaded, not a transformed text version of it. Users should be able to install or resolve packages from repositories that omit charset metadata without seeing false metadata hash mismatches caused solely by response decoding.

constraints.grounded: The change should affect metadata hash computation only, preserve the existing hash algorithms and comparison flow, and avoid introducing new behavior for unrelated artifact downloads or non-metadata validation paths.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to preventing encoding-related false mismatches during metadata verification and should not change how other package files are fetched, hashed, or validated.

behavior: Metadata hash verification now derives the digest from the raw bytes of the metadata HTTP response.
Metadata responses without charset information no longer rely on implicit text decoding before hash calculation.
A metadata file whose decoded text would not round-trip to the original bytes can still pass hash verification when the downloaded byte content matches the published hash.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry downloads package metadata from a repository that omits charset information, it should compute the metadata hash from the original response bytes.
When the published metadata hash matches the downloaded metadata bytes, Poetry should accept the metadata even if decoding the response text would have produced different bytes.
When the downloaded metadata bytes do not match the published metadata hash, Poetry should continue to treat the metadata as failing hash verification.

task_7.title: Allow `poetry add` in unnamed non-package projects
task_7.description: Poetry 1.8.2 fixes a regression in `poetry add` for non-package-mode projects that do not declare a project name. The command should treat the project name as optional in that configuration and continue normal dependency addition behavior instead of failing during command processing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry add` works for projects running in non-package mode even when no project name is configured.

expectation.grounded: When a project is configured with `package-mode = false` and `tool.poetry.name` is absent, `poetry add` should not fail because the command attempts to read or normalize a missing project name. The command should proceed with normal dependency addition behavior. If `tool.poetry.name` is present, `poetry add` should continue using its normalized form where relevant.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to add dependencies in non-package projects without being forced to define a package name. The add command should accept unnamed project metadata in that mode and behave the same as a normal dependency add operation.

constraints.grounded: Do not require a synthetic or placeholder project name for `poetry add` to work in non-package mode. Preserve existing `poetry add` behavior for projects that already define `tool.poetry.name`, including normalized-name handling when a name exists.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only remove the unnecessary failure caused by an absent project name. It should not change normal add behavior for projects that are already valid and named.

behavior: `poetry add` no longer assumes that `tool.poetry.name` is always present before processing dependency additions.
In non-package mode, an omitted project name is treated as an allowed absent value rather than as a command-stopping error condition.
When a project name is configured, `poetry add` continues to use the normalized project name behavior it already applied before the fix.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project configured for non-package mode with no declared project name, when `poetry add <dependency>` is run, the command should complete without failing due to the missing name.
When `poetry add` succeeds in that configuration, it should carry out the usual dependency addition outcome expected from the command.
Given a project that does declare a name, when `poetry add` is run, it should continue to behave consistently with existing named-project handling.

task_8.title: Correct Poetry install guidance for package-mode
task_8.description: Poetry 1.8.2 corrects the install-time guidance shown for dependency-management-only projects so it references the finalized `package-mode` setting instead of outdated non-package mode wording.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the install-time guidance for projects that should not be installed as packages points users to the supported `package-mode` configuration instead of obsolete non-package mode terminology.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry emits the existing warning during `poetry install` about not installing the current project as a package, it must continue to offer `--no-root` for skipping installation of the current project and must direct dependency-management-only users to disable package mode with the public `package-mode` setting in `pyproject.toml`, rather than referring to a `non-package` operating mode.
expectation.conceptual: Users who see the install warning should be guided with the current, supported configuration name for dependency-only workflows, so the message is accurate and actionable without relying on outdated terminology.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the condition under which the install warning appears or the availability of the `--no-root` guidance. The fix should preserve the warning flow and only align the configuration hint with Poetry's public package-mode setting.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the existing install behavior and warning scenario intact while correcting the configuration advice so it matches the supported product surface.

behavior: When the existing `poetry install` warning about not installing the current project is shown, it continues to present `--no-root` as the option for skipping installation of the current project.
The same warning now tells users who want dependency management without packaging to disable package mode via the `package-mode` setting in `pyproject.toml`.
The warning no longer describes this workflow using an outdated `non-package` operating mode name.
acceptance_criteria: When a user encounters the existing install warning during `poetry install`, the output should still be presented as a warning and should continue to mention `--no-root` for avoiding installation of the current project.
When the warning explains how to use Poetry only for dependency management, it should direct the user to disable package mode using the public `package-mode` setting in `pyproject.toml`.
When users read the warning, it should not reference a `non-package` operating mode or any obsolete setting name for this workflow.

task_5.title: Improve lazy-wheel fallback diagnostics
task_5.description: Poetry 1.8.2 improves lazy-wheel failure handling during wheel metadata inspection. When lazy-wheel cannot be used for a repository host, Poetry now treats any lazy-wheel unsupported condition as a fallback signal, disables the optimization for that host, and records the reason in debug logs before continuing with the normal wheel download path.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when wheel metadata cannot be retrieved through Poetry's lazy-wheel optimization, the affected repository host falls back cleanly and the reason is visible in debug output instead of only handling a narrow subset of lazy-wheel failure conditions.

expectation.grounded: During wheel package inspection, if lazy metadata retrieval raises `LazyWheelUnsupportedError`, Poetry should handle it as a lazy-wheel fallback condition rather than only handling `HTTPRangeRequestUnsupported`. It should emit a debug-level log identifying that lazy-wheel support is being disabled for the relevant host and include the error reason, then continue through the standard downloaded-wheel metadata path. Successful lazy-wheel metadata retrieval should still mark the host as range-request capable. A fallback should only default host capability to unsupported when no prior successful range-request support has already been established for that host.
expectation.conceptual: Any repository-specific lazy-wheel failure should degrade gracefully. Poetry should stop using the lazy-wheel optimization for the affected host, log enough debug information to explain why it was disabled, and continue resolving package metadata through the regular wheel download flow.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful lazy-wheel behavior for hosts that return usable metadata. Do not convert a `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` into a hard package-inspection failure when normal wheel download can still proceed. Do not overwrite previously established evidence that a host supports range requests for other URLs merely because one lazy-wheel attempt was unsupported.
constraints.conceptual: Keep lazy-wheel opportunistic: working hosts should continue to benefit from it, unsupported cases should fall back safely, and one unsupported response should not unnecessarily degrade known-good host behavior.

behavior: Catching `LazyWheelUnsupportedError` during lazy wheel metadata retrieval now triggers fallback, not only `HTTPRangeRequestUnsupported`.
When fallback is triggered, Poetry emits a debug-level log stating that lazy-wheel support is being disabled for the affected repository host and why.
After a lazy-wheel unsupported condition, Poetry proceeds with the regular wheel download and metadata extraction path.
The affected host is only defaulted to unsupported for range-based lazy-wheel retrieval if no prior successful range-request support was already known.
When lazy-wheel metadata retrieval succeeds, Poetry still records the host as supporting range requests and returns metadata without falling back.
acceptance_criteria: Given lazy-wheel is enabled for a repository host with unknown range support, when wheel metadata retrieval encounters any `LazyWheelUnsupportedError`, then Poetry should disable lazy-wheel for that host and continue by inspecting the wheel through the normal download path.

Given debug logging is enabled, when Poetry disables lazy-wheel for a host after a lazy-wheel unsupported condition, then the logs should identify the host and include the reason that caused the fallback.
When lazy-wheel metadata retrieval succeeds for a host, it should continue to use the lazy metadata path and preserve that host as range-request capable.

Given a host was already known to support range requests for some URLs, when a different lazy-wheel attempt on that host is unsupported, then Poetry should fall back for that operation without erasing the previously known support state.
